questions.question: Before changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before you move into the other lane, quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?
questions.explanation: In an accident, stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop serious bleeding. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the police car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel when stopped by police. Tell any passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: You are angry after an incident at work. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
Stop at a bar for drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to cool off before driving. Driving while emotional is very dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should a driver do?

options.text: Stop at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes—another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.explanation: Drivers must follow traffic signals, except when a police officer is directing traffic. When an officer is present, follow their directions instead of the signal.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving:
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a dangerous distraction. It makes you take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is being dangerous, stay calm and create distance between your vehicles. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. You must stop if:
questions.explanation: Always stop before railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a person signals you to stop, or a train is visible or close. If you are unsure whether it is safe to cross, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are only found in construction zones.
Are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings give drivers important information. They help drivers position their vehicles correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means an action is not allowed. This sign means right turns are not permitted at this location.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right of way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if a sign does not prohibit it.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly whenever you drive.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the new lane is clear before moving into it.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Turns off the seat belt warning light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should fit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: Before driving after taking a non-prescription drug, you should:
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving ability. Check the label for warnings about medicines for colds or allergies. If unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive.

questions.question: To drive safely based on your physical condition, you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and have regular check-ups.
Know how medicine affects your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay in the right lane to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Stay farther away from the car in front of you.
Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see. Take steps to stay safe and protect other drivers on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means the action is not allowed. This sign means you cannot make U-turns.

questions.question: When is passing not allowed?
questions.explanation: You cannot pass other vehicles on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These places are unsafe for passing.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and let them cross first. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use turn signals, obey speed limits, and leave extra time for your trip.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going downhill than smaller vehicles.
Have a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.
